application.desc: GROBID - A machine learning software for extracting information from scholarly documents

div.p: This paper presents a new real-time scheduling protocol for semantic concurrency control of objectoriented database systems. Although recent results about object-oriented serializability are efficient in the semantic concurrency contorol, these results still lack in real-time schedulability. Our new scheduling protocol takes into accounts not only object-oriented serializability but also real-time schedulability. Our protocol also has capabilities to avoid "the worst casen in which the early invoked transaction waits for long time, and avoid deadlock in the scheduling of the object-oriented database systems.

div.head: Introduction
div.p: Real-time database is one of the most remarkable research field in the database world [6]. Especially, transaction processing and concurrency control require additional mechanism of real-time property to improve schedulability of database manipulation [ 7 ] . The semantic concurrency control which is more flexible than classic concurrency control requires schedulability for efficient transaction management. This new concurrency control has been explored to cope with cooperative transactions, long duration transaction and object-oriented database.

Based on the open nested transaction [1.2] which is a transaction model for nested relational database and object-oriented database, Neuhold, Weikum and Rakow has succeeded in relaxing traditional concept of the serializability by introducing commutativity. However, there still exists problem that the requested subtransaction may wait till commit of top-level transaction to which the preceding subtransaction belongs, which is called "the worst case " phenomena. E'uthermore. in the semantic concurrency control, as deadlock is inevitable in which subtransaction waits for unlock of another subtransaction in cyclic manner, efficient scheduling avoiding deadlock is requested. The purpose of this paper is to present real-time shedding for semantic concurrency control of object-oriented database system in order to obtain schedulability and deadlock avoidance by introducing priority of process scheduling instead of retainedlock of the semantic concurrency control. Organization of this paper is outlined. Section2 describes semantic concurrency control in connection with schedulability.

Section3 presents a real-time scheduling for the semantic concurrency control of the object-oriented database system. Especially, we present a rule, an algorithm and their example of the real-time scheduling. Section4 presents several theorems that show object-oriented serializability of our approach. Section5 concludes.

div.head: Semantic Concurrency Control
div.p: As preliminary of our real-time scheduling for semantic concurrency control of object-oriented database system. this section describes structure of transaction model in a sense of message passing and outline of the semantic concurrency control.

div.head: 2-1 Transact ion Model
div.p: A transaction model of the object-oriented database system is delineated. Every object that some subtransactions access has its particular method. In general. a method of transaction Ta has the following structure :

Due to message passings, object, 3.Tz.~ ( j = 1,2), transaction TI sequentially invokes two subtransactions Ta 1 and Ta.2. Similarly, the subtransaction Tz.1 includes message passing object, 1 k.Tz.1 .k, subtransaction Tz. 1 also invokes another subtransaction Tt.1 k Thus, the transaction consists of a tree in which every parentchildren relationship corresponds to invoke-invoked subtranctions. Direction of invocation is from the root to leaves of the transaction tree, while direction of execution is from leaves to the root. When there exist two subtransactions which are children of the same parent subtransaction, left subtransaction is invoked first and executed. where there is no parallelism between left and right subtransactions. To cope with long duration transaction, cooperative transaction considering CAD and groupware, coexistence of several transactions is allowed. Therefore, different subtransactions belonging to two transactions also exist which access the same object.

div.head: 2-2 Semantic Concurrency Control
div.p: A semantic concurrency control in object-oriented database system has been investigated by Rakow,Gu and Neuhold [4] and Muth,Rakow,Weikum et.a1.[3] based on a concept of object-oriented serializability . The architecture of this semantic concurrency control is described in detail. The decision of execution of the subtransaction depends on being commutativity/conflicting between subtransactions accessing the same object. In case of commutativity between subtransactions, additional condition is whether descendant subtransactions of the above two subtransactions commute or conflict. If two decendants commute, ordering of execution between two subtransactions is independent of that which transaction is executed first. If two descendants conflict, and if the preceding descendant has not been committed, the requested subtransaction cannot be locked. If two descendants conflict, and if the preceding descendant has already been committed, the requested subtransaction can enter critical section, that is, locked. In case of conflicting between subtransactions, the requested subtransaction is executed after the commit of the preceding subtransaction. According to the protocol of this semantic concurrency control [3], once a subtransaction has been commited, that is, unlocked, that; subtransaction is converted into retained-lock hill completion of the transaction to which the committed subtransaction belongs. When two transactions differ to which two conflicting subtransactions respectively belong, executing order between two subtransactions is according to definition of the object-oriented serializability. The definition of the object-oriented seializability is such that, for any object schedule, there exists an equivalent serial object schedule [4]. Consequently, executing order is decided corresponding to invoking order between transactions. However, in case of conflicting, this protocol has " the worst case " in which the requested subtransaction may wait till the commit of top-level transaction of the precedeing subtransaction [3]. Furthermore, there exists possibility of deadlock occurrence when this protocol of the semantic concurrency control is applied. Consequently, this semantic concurrency control requires real-time sche duling to avoid " the worst case " and deadlock for efficient schedulability of the object-oriented database system.

div.head: Real-Time Scheduling
div.p: This section presents rule and algorithm for real-time scheduling of the semantic concurrency control in objectoriented database system. In addition to these ones, we present an example which shows effectiveness of this algorithm. At first, we propose a rule along with terminologies of the real-time scheduling part of which we owe to the literature [5].

div.head: 3-1 Rule
div.p: The run-time system implies a system which executes and completes transaction, and compares priorities of transactions under our algorithm, protocol, which we'll propose later. Notation Tn stands for a run-time system which supervises execution and completion for transaction/subtransaction in which T n is a top-level. Due to definition of the object-oriented serializablity, executing order between conflicting subtransactions should obey order of invoked transactions. For realization of realtime scheduling for semantic concurrenEy control bet ween t r ansactions/sub tr ansactions, we design t he following rule.

0 The priority is assigned to every transaction. The priority of every transaction is invoked order of top level transaction. 0 The executing order between conflicting subtransactions is according to the priorities. In other words, a subtransaction is blocked and cannot be executed at when the subtransaction has not been completed due to existence of conflicting transactions with higher priorities. 0 The executing order between commuting subtransactions can be decided using priority ceiling. The subtransaction trying to execute is blocked by subtransactions ( now interrupted ) with higher priority ceilings. Priotirty ceiling is defined as the priority of the highest priority transaction that may access this object. Due to uncertain assignment for execution between commuting subtransactions, the priority ceiling has been introduced.

Furthermore, if there exist some subtransactions with same highest priorities, make feasible the subtransaction which was invoked first.

div.head: Theoretical Results of Real-Time Scheduling
div.p: This section presents theoretical results summarized as three theorems which show effective properties about our rule and algorithm for real-time scheduling of the semantic concurrency control explored in the previous section.

Three theorems are about guarantee of object-oriented serializability by our algorithm, possibility of avoidance for " the worst case " in the semantic concurrency control and finally avoidance for deadlock inherent to locking of the database.
Theorem 1 The object-oriented serializabalaty holds zn o w algorathm.

Proof Since the executing order between conflicting subtransactions is according to the priorities, then transaction dependency relation of object schedule holds, where the transaction dependency relation is that, if Ti precedes Tj, then a, precedes another as, where ak is subtransaction in Tk ( k = t , 1) and a, conflicts with a3.

In fact, since priority or priority ceiling of subtransactions in the transaction T i is not lower than the priority of Ti, subtransactions in the proceeding transactions Ta+n(n 2 1) cannot preempt these subtransactions in T z . Due to this transaction dependency relation, equivalent serial object schedule exist for any object schedule, where two object schedules have the same transaction dependency relation, that is, equivalent.

Example We stress correctness of the object-oriented serializability in our algorithm about real-time scheduling of the concurrency control. It is sufficient to show that execution-order among conflicting transactions which access the same object follows invoke-order of transactions. For example, let's look at an object P. The execution-order of subtransactions accessing an object P is such as T1.l.l (at t o ) , T2.1.1 (at t 1 ) . This excution-order corresponds to invoke-order such as TI, T2. F'uthermore, look at an object C . The execution-order of subtransactions accessing an object C is such as 0 (at t o ) , @ (at t 7 ) , 0, which corresponds to invoke-order T1, T2, T3.
Theorem 2 Our algorithm can avotd the worst case " of the semantzc concurrency control.

Proof Since the executing order can be decided by comparing priori ties between concerned subtransactions, "the worst case" in which the requested subtransaction may wait for a long time till completion of top-level transaction of the preceding subtransaction never occurs.

0 Remark 3 The traditional semantic concurrency control allows execution of subtransactions in the transaction which is invoked later as long as commutativity holds. Consequently remaining subtransactions in the early invoked transaction may wait for long till commit of subtransactions in the late invoked transaction, which is called "the worst case". Our scheduling of the semantic concurrency control can avoid such problem due to priority based properties.
Theorem 3 OUT algorzthm can avoid deadlock.

Proof Since our algorithm does not employ any locks, and every subtransaction is managed with the highest priority in turn, the deadlock in which a subtransaction waits for another subtransaction in cyclic manner cannot occur. Consequentlly, our algorithm can avoid deadlock.

div.head: 5 Conclusion
div.p: In this paper, we have presented a method and algorithm which enables real-time scheduling of the semantic concurrency control in the object-oriented database systems by introducing priority of the process scheduling in the operationg system. Our approach can be regarded as realization of scheduling of the concurrency control based on combination of database and operationg system. Effectiveness of our proposal for transaction management has been verified by proving object-oriented serializability, avoidance of " the worst case " and deadlock. Implementation of our approach is the future work.
